messages:
sec-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Spike in rapid-successful MFA pushes for multiple accounts across NA -> EU within 45s. 12 affected sessions. Possible MFA fatigue or abuse. logs: https://logs.redwood.example/alerts/1778881234
jess (sec-lead): I'm looking. which identities? any service accounts? :thinking_face:
liz (oncall): seeing pattern: user + browser user-agent flips and same device fingerprints, but different IPs. 7 human accounts, 5 machine/service-account-like.
omar (infra): service-account  svc-ingest-prod shows many accepted pushes in <30s window, token refreshes succeeded after accept. KMS key rotation completed ~22:14 UTC earlier, checking correlation.
patrick (sre): running quick containment: can we suspend refresh-token issuance for affected clients?
jess (sec-lead): yes do that. Patrick - suspend `refresh` for svc-ingest-prod and rotate its client secret. Liz - collect raw push events and push metadata (app version, push prompt text). Omar - check KMS audit for key use around that time. Maria - draft customer notif if any external-facing creds affected.
patrick (sre): running: `curl -X POST https://internal-auth/sessions/revoke -d '{"client_id":"svc-ingest-prod","type":"refresh"}'` -> 202 accepted. Will rotate client secret now.
liz (oncall): raw push events: `user_agent: iOS/16.4`, `push_text: "Redwood login"`, `accept_time_ms` clustered ~12000ms after push. Seems like users are accepting quickly. Also note `push_origin: push-service.eu1` for NA IPs.
omar (infra): KMS audit: no unauthorized key access, but key rotation completed and re-encryption jobs spiked, which triggered a lot of background auth refreshes for long-lived clients. That may have caused prompt storms.
jess (sec-lead): ok plausible cause: rotation-caused reauth + benign push fatigue. But service accounts accepting pushes is suspicious. Which of the 5 are true service accounts?
liz (oncall): svc-ingest-prod and svc-analytics-runner look machine-ish. Others are user emails.
patrick (sre): svc-ingest-prod secret rotated and new secret deployed to helm canary. svc-analytics-runner flagged for immediate secret rotation and disabled interactive pushes (set MFA mode to `push with confirm`).
maria (cs): preparing template: short notice, no data exfil, recommending password reset if user concerned, and reminding to check device prompts. Will post to status.redwood for affected orgs if any.
jess (sec-lead): action list TL;DR: 1) rotate & revoke refresh tokens for flagged clients (patrick) 2) temporary throttle push service to cross-region pushes (omar) 3) audit KMS rotation path/automation (omar + jess) 4) RBAC check on service accounts, remove `interactive-login` permission if not needed (jess + infra) 5) update MFA prompt text to include org name + flow context (product + devex followup) 6) postmortem and customer comms (maria).
omar (infra): implemented rate limit on `push-service.eu1` for clients originating from NA IPs -> config `max_cross_region_push_rate: 2/min` pushed.
liz (oncall): adding logs to incident channel and saving evidence: `curl -s https://logs/api/1778881234/export > /tmp/1778881234.json`
jess (sec-lead): good. Marking severity low-medium for now since no sign of credential theft. We'll escalate if more accounts show refresh success after revocation.
patrick (sre): verified: revoked tokens show up as 401 on subsequent refresh attempts. svc-ingest-prod now failing with 401 until new secret roll completes.
maria (cs): sent preliminary notice to 3 affected customers with remediation steps. No public status needed.
jess (sec-lead): follow-ups for postmortem: - timeline + root cause hypothesis - quantify affected sessions and orgs - remediation (RBAC changes, client secret rotation policy, push throttles) - add automation test that simulates KMS rotation to detect push storms. Assign owners?
omar (infra): I’ll own KMS rotation automation tests.
patrick (sre): I’ll own RBAC review for service accounts and rotate any high-risk secrets.
maria (cs): I’ll finalize customer comms and the postmortem summary for CSMs.
liz (oncall): I’ll attach logs and screenshots to the ticket.
jess (sec-lead): thanks team. leaving action items in JIRA INC-4321. tagging for visibility @product @devex for prompt wording change. :lock: If anything changes ping here.
sec-bot: Incident INC-4321 created and assigned: jess (sec-lead). Priority: P2. https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-4321
jess (sec-lead): closing thread here unless we see more failures. good job. :thumbsup:
